Either only cross edges are tight, producing constant class values, or one class attains separation s; cross constraints force the other class into [s-1,1], and tight connectivity forces all values to {0,s} and {s-1,1}. All candidate profiles are feasible. The exact identity Q=sS-b(s-1) completes the variance square, proving the two-orientation discrepancy equality and all optimizers. At \(s=3/2\) the intervals [3k,3k+b] cover each integer from 0 to 3a+b for \(b\ge2\), giving delta=0 or 1/4 by parity. Endpoint limits are computed directly; exact rational spanning-tree enumeration independently checks 18 small examples and rational midpoint/endpoint tables.

value.rationale: The sharp probability variance is the natural Lipschitz Poincare constant of an entire family interpolating equilateral and graph metrics. The result converts an N-dimensional continuum optimization to an exact two-integer arithmetic discrepancy with an O(N) evaluation algorithm, classifies every maximizer, and discovers a closed parity-sensitive midpoint law for all cluster sizes. These are structural exact invariants and equality cases, not ad hoc finite instances or mere naming changes.
